propositions: A single pending queue entry disables the O(1) fast-path cache marker store-wide, forcing full store directory walks on every subsequent write until the pending set empties.
The gate marker is written only when a full scan finds no pending entries, creating a binary trigger that does not scale with backlog size or pending entry count.

The live-set marker design records ticket ids with enqueued (non-DONE) entries during each full scan, enabling subsequent probes to reduce only those entries (O(backlog)) instead of rescanning the entire store (O(store)).
Scoped probes with a valid live-set marker do not refresh the marker's written_ns timestamp, preserving the TTL bound measured from the last full walk.
Every queue append clears the marker, ensuring new entries are visible and not hidden behind a stale live set.
The extracted _scan_pending helper maintains the f400 service-order sort (not_before_ns, ticket_id) for both full-walk and scoped-walk paths, guaranteeing ordering parity.
